title: Momentum (MOM)
summary: The plain price difference between this bar and the bar a fixed number of bars back, drawn as a line around zero.
description:
Momentum is the simplest measure of how fast price is moving. On every bar it takes the chosen source and subtracts the value of the same source `length` bars earlier. The answer is in price units: on a market trading near 60,000 a reading of 500 means price is 500 higher than it was `length` bars ago.

There is no smoothing and no scaling, so the line reacts as soon as price does and carries all of its noise. The first `length` bars have no reading, because there is no bar that far back to compare with, and the line starts once there is.
howToRead:
Above zero, price is higher than it was `length` bars ago; below zero, it is lower. The further the line is from zero, the faster the move. A line that keeps rising while price rises says the advance is speeding up, and a line that turns down while price is still climbing says the advance is slowing, which often comes before a pause or a turn.

Because the reading is in price units, its size depends on the instrument's price level, so compare it only with its own history on the same chart. A single large bar entering or leaving the window can jump the line, which is the cost of having no smoothing.

settings.label: Length
settings.description: How many bars back the comparison reaches. A short length follows every swing; a long one shows the broader trend of the move.

settings.label: Source
settings.description: The price series compared with its own earlier value. Close is the default; hl2 and the other blends soften bars with long wicks.

faq.q: Why is the start of the chart blank?
faq.a: The first reading needs a bar `length` bars back. Until the chart has that many bars there is nothing to subtract, so the line starts on bar `length`.

faq.q: How is this different from Rate of Change Percentage?
faq.a: Momentum is the raw difference in price units. A percentage rate of change divides that difference by the older price, so its readings compare across instruments and price levels.

faq.q: Does a zero cross mean anything?
faq.a: A cross above zero means price has just risen above where it was `length` bars ago, and a cross below means it has fallen under it. It describes the move; it does not forecast the next one.
